info.text: English for Aviation Maintenance — Unit 17: Coordinating a component removal and installation (CEFR B2). Split by skill: listening, reading, use of English, vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Which figure do Rob and Lena open in the illustrated parts catalogue to find the generator?

generalfeedback.text: Rob says: "Open figure twenty-four eleven zero-one." The generator sits in the middle of figure 24-11-01.

feedback.text: Correct — the figure the generator sits in.
The middle and last groups are the wrong way round — listen again.
That is a different ATA chapter; the figure is 24-11-01.
The last two digits are swapped; it is 24-11-01.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What item number is the integrated drive generator in the figure? Type the number only.

generalfeedback.text: Lena confirms: "The generator is item number forty in the figure." The answer is 40.

feedback.text: Correct — item 40.
Item 45 is the mounting clamp, not the generator.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. True or false: they remove the mounting bolt first, before the electrical connector.

generalfeedback.text: False. The electrical connector comes off first; the mounting bolt is the last item, because the component is heavy once the bolt is out.

feedback.text: No — the connector is disconnected first; the bolt is last.
Correct — connector first, mounting bolt last.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. What does Lena fit on the open plug straight away, so no dirt gets in?

generalfeedback.text: Rob says: "Fit the blanking cap now, so no dirt gets into the electrical connector." A blanking cap closes the open plug.

feedback.text: Correct — it keeps contamination out of the plug.
The bonding lead is the earth strap, not a cap for the plug.
A warning tag marks a state; it does not close a plug.
A torque seal is a paint mark on a bolt, not a plug cap.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. What is the torque value for the mounting bolt, in newton metres? Type the number only.

generalfeedback.text: The task card gives thirty-four newton metres; the wrench clicks at thirty-four. The answer is 34.

feedback.text: Correct — 34 N·m.
The digits are reversed — it is 34, not 43.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. Why do they add a torque seal across the bolt head?

generalfeedback.text: Rob says: "Add a torque seal, so the next shift can see the bolt was torqued." The seal is a visible check for the next inspector.

answer.text: So the next shift can see the bolt was torqued.

feedback.text: Correct — a torque seal is visible evidence of torque.

answer.text: To keep dirt out of the open electrical connector plug.

feedback.text: That is the job of a blanking cap, not a torque seal.

answer.text: Because the bonding lead needs a second securing point.

feedback.text: The seal has nothing to do with the bonding lead.

answer.text: To give the oil lines an extra layer of leak protection.

feedback.text: The oil lines are sealed by their unions and lockwire, not the torque seal.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 again (the handover voicemail). True or false: the functional test was good and the generator is serviceable.

generalfeedback.text: True. Rob says the functional test was good, so the generator is serviceable and the task card is signed.

feedback.text: Correct — test good, unit serviceable, card signed.
Listen again — the test was good and the unit is serviceable.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 again. The integrated drive generator was changed on which engine? Type the engine number only.

generalfeedback.text: Rob says the IDG was changed on engine one, on tail YL-BBX. The answer is 1.

feedback.text: Correct — engine one.
Bay two is where the aircraft sits; the engine is number one.

questiontext.text:
Read this Service Bulletin extract, then answer.

SB 24-0071 — Integrated drive generator. This bulletin introduces improved generator part number 761782D. Operators must comply within 600 flight hours from receipt. Until compliance, part number 761782C remains approved for continued use.

By when must operators comply with SB 24-0071?

generalfeedback.text: The bulletin sets the compliance window at 600 flight hours from receipt. Until then, the old part number 761782C is still approved.

feedback.text: Correct — 600 flight hours from receipt.

answer.text: Immediately, before the next flight of the aircraft.

feedback.text: No — the SB allows 600 flight hours, and 761782C stays approved until then.

answer.text: Within thirty calendar days of receiving the bulletin.

feedback.text: The window is measured in flight hours, not calendar days.

answer.text: Only at the next scheduled base maintenance check.

feedback.text: The bulletin gives a flight-hour limit, not a check reference.

questiontext.text:
Read this Minimum Equipment List (MEL) extract, then answer.

MEL 24-11 IDG: One integrated drive generator may be inoperative provided the associated generator is disconnected and an INOP placard is fitted. Category C — rectify within 10 days.

True or false: under this MEL, the aircraft may keep flying with one IDG inoperative if the generator is disconnected and placarded.

generalfeedback.text: True. The MEL permits dispatch with one IDG inoperative, provided it is disconnected and an INOP placard is fitted, with rectification within 10 days (Category C).

feedback.text: Correct — the conditions are disconnect and placard, rectify within 10 days.
The MEL does allow it under the stated conditions.

questiontext.text:
Read this technical-log entry, then answer.

Reported: ENG 1 GEN caution on climb. Action: IDG (item 40) removed and replaced, part number 761782C. Torqued to value, lockwire and torque seal fitted. Functional test satisfactory. A/C released to service.

What did the technician do about the reported GEN caution?

generalfeedback.text: The action line records that the IDG was removed and replaced, then torqued, lockwired, sealed and tested before release.

feedback.text: Correct — the IDG was removed and replaced, then tested.

answer.text: Reset the caution and returned the aircraft with no part change.

feedback.text: No — the log clearly records a part change, not a reset.

answer.text: Disconnected the generator and fitted an inoperative placard.

feedback.text: That would be an MEL deferral; here the unit was actually replaced.

answer.text: Cleaned the electrical connector and re-ran the functional test.

feedback.text: The log shows a full removal and replacement, not just cleaning.

questiontext.text:
Read this AMM torque table note, then answer.

AMM 24-11-01, Table 401: IDG mounting bolt — torque 34 N·m. Fit lockwire after torque. Do not exceed the stated value; if the value is exceeded, replace the bolt.

True or false: if the mounting bolt is tightened past 34 N·m, the table says to replace the bolt.

generalfeedback.text: True. The note says do not exceed 34 N·m, and if the value is exceeded, replace the bolt — over-torque can damage the fastener.

feedback.text: Correct — exceed the value, replace the bolt.
Read the last line again — an over-torqued bolt must be replaced.

questiontext.text:
Read this task-card sign-off rule, then answer.

Sign-off: Sign the task card only when the installation and the functional test are both complete. The unit is serviceable when the test is satisfactory.

When may the technician sign the task card?

generalfeedback.text: The rule is explicit: sign only when the installation and the functional test are both complete.

answer.text: When the install and the test are both complete.

feedback.text: Correct — both the installation and the test must be finished.

answer.text: As soon as the new component is lifted onto the clamp.

feedback.text: Too early — the torque, lockwire and test still have to be done.

answer.text: Before the removal, so the paperwork is ready in advance.

feedback.text: You never sign before the work; the test must pass first.

answer.text: Once the old unit has been tagged and taken from the bay.

feedback.text: Tagging the old unit is not the sign-off condition; the test is.

questiontext.text: Rewrite as an active imperative (STE). "The electrical connector must be disconnected." Type the missing verb: ______ the electrical connector.

generalfeedback.text: STE names the action and starts with the verb: Disconnect the electrical connector. Drop "must be".

feedback.text: Correct — verb first.
Correct.
Start with the plain verb "Disconnect".

questiontext.text: Rewrite as an active imperative (STE). "It is necessary to fit the blanking cap." Type the missing verb: ______ the blanking cap.

generalfeedback.text: Delete the empty "It is necessary to" and start with the verb: Fit the blanking cap.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
The verb is "Fit".

questiontext.text: Rewrite as an active imperative (STE). "The mounting bolt is to be torqued to 34." Type the missing verb: ______ the mounting bolt to 34.

generalfeedback.text: Active and verb-first: Torque the mounting bolt to 34. The value stays with the object.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
The verb is "Torque".

questiontext.text: Complete with the bank term. The calibrated tool that tightens a fastener to a specified torque value is a ______ ______.

generalfeedback.text: The tool set to the value and used until it clicks is the torque wrench.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
The term is "torque wrench".

questiontext.text: Complete with the bank term. The IPC data that shows which aircraft a part actually applies to is the ______.

generalfeedback.text: The column that confirms the part fits this tail is the effectivity.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
The term is "effectivity".

questiontext.text: Rewrite as an active imperative (STE). "A functional test must be carried out." Type the missing verb (one word or two): ______ a functional test.

generalfeedback.text: Verb-first: Run a functional test (or Carry out a functional test). Both are accepted.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Correct.
Correct.
Use "Run" or "Carry out".

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: lockwire = wire that stops a fastener turning loose; blanking cap = closes an open pipe or plug; bonding lead = earth strap to the airframe; torque seal = paint mark showing a bolt was torqued; effectivity = which aircraft a part applies to.

answer.text: wire that stops a fastener turning loose
a cap that closes an open pipe or plug
the strap that earths the case to the airframe
a paint mark showing a bolt was torqued
which aircraft a part applies to

questiontext.text: Match each term to its meaning.

generalfeedback.text: serviceable = fit for use; unserviceable = not fit, must be repaired; item number = identifies a part in a figure; part number = the maker's unique reference; task card = the printed list of steps.

answer.text: not fit for use; must be repaired
identifies a part within an IPC figure
the maker's unique reference for a part
the printed list of job steps

name.text: U17 V3 verb to noun collocation

questiontext.text: Match each verb to the noun it goes with in the unit.

generalfeedback.text: check the effectivity; torque the mounting bolt; fit a blanking cap; run a functional test; sign the task card.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its meaning.

generalfeedback.text: removal = taking a component off; installation = fitting a component on; component = a single unit removed as one; fastener = a bolt, nut or screw; electrical connector = the plug to the aircraft wiring.

answer.text: taking a component off the aircraft
fitting a component onto the aircraft
a single unit removed and replaced as one
a bolt, nut or screw that holds parts together
the plug that joins the unit to the aircraft wiring
